meaning: When capability-document bytes are not the canonical encoding of representable limits, the closed decoder returns nothing — truncation, oversize fields, and trailing bytes are all rejected with the same fail-closed posture as node bytes, and a successful decode's input is exactly the canonical encoding of its result.
oracle: Capability documents are eight canonical bytes — two big-endian 32-bit naturals, the key-count limit then the blob-byte limit — parsed by a closed decoder that rejects truncation and trailing content; a successful decode's input is exactly the canonical encoding of its result.
